subject: Fixed predictors/random effects for discrimination parameters in mixedmirt

messages.author: 394838c3712aced6
messages.subject: Fixed predictors/random effects for discrimination parameters in mixedmirt
parts:
I'm interested in using mixedmirt to estimate a MIMIC-type model, where a continuous predictor (a personality trait) predicts both the item intercepts as well as the item discrimination/slope parameters. 

A model like:  P(x = 1 | θ, ψ) = 1 / (1 + exp(-1 * [θ * (a + ψζ) +  ψβ))

For example, I might have a set of cognitive test items, and I want to model the effects of test anxiety scores on both item difficulties and discrimination parameters.

I could potentially extend this to include random effects as well ala https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11336-013-9360-2.pdf

Can item discrimination models currently be estimated in mirt? From the ?mixedmirt documentation, it seems like only intercept models can be specified. 

Using the `lr.fixed` and `lr.random` arguments, I could specify a model for θ, but that is a slightly different specification than specifying a model for a directly (e.g., if I wanted to estimate both non-uniform DIF and latent trait group differences).

Thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fixed predictors/random effects for discrimination parameters in mixedmirt
parts:
Unfortunately, mixedmirt() is currently not capable of treating the slopes as random effects for this purpose of this type of decomposition (only the theta and intercept terms are currently supported). It's of course possible to modify the program to do this type of decomposition, but it would take a non-trivial amount of time (which, given the new stressors these days, I don't have much of anymore.....). I'll add it to the long-list of TODOs for the package, but I wouldn't expect to see this feature for quite some time. Sorry in advance.

Phil
